model.inputs: one immutable requirement and one immutable advertisement
model.client_labels: opaque illustrative strings, not assertions about named products

version_grammar.components: canonical decimal integers 0..999999 with no leading zeroes
version_grammar.range: min_inclusive is required; max_exclusive is nullable
version_grammar.excluded: no prerelease, build metadata, wildcard, caret, tilde, alias, or inferred compatibility

result_precedence: otherwise any unknown absence produces indeterminate

semantics.protocol: protocol ID is exact and the advertised version must fall in the required range
semantics.capabilities: every required ID must exist at a satisfying advertised version
semantics.interaction_modes_any: empty means unconstrained; otherwise at least one exact label must intersect
semantics.content_types_any: empty means unconstrained; otherwise at least one exact label must intersect
semantics.tools: every required tool ID must satisfy version and exact input/output schema labels
semantics.partial: absence is unknown only when advertisement.completeness is partial; present contradictory facts remain definite
semantics.extensions: explicit extension objects are retained as inputs but ignored by evaluation
semantics.extras: extra advertised capabilities, tools, modes, and content types are ignored
semantics.ordering: input list order never affects the verdict; output facts use Unicode scalar ordering

canonical_json.numbers: safe integers only; floats, exponent forms, negative zero, and non-finite values reject
canonical_json.strings: valid Unicode scalar values only; no normalization or locale folding

invariants: evaluation is a pure function of the supplied scenario
no output contains a score, rank, route, provider choice, or dispatch decision
partial completeness changes absence only, never a positive contradiction
matched output lists are sorted and duplicate-free
mismatch facts are sorted by code, path, expected, actual, and certainty
permuting semantically set-like input lists cannot change the canonical output

requirements: JavaScript and Python parser classifications independently match golden expected codes
JavaScript and Python validation classifications independently match golden expected codes, including label and list limits
JavaScript and Python complete verdicts are byte-identical
paired set-like input permutations produce byte-identical projections
all mismatch facts are canonically ordered
all normalized matched lists are ordered and duplicate-free
result precedence agrees with mismatch certainty

non_claims: no live discovery, registry, directory, cache, freshness, TTL, or network behavior
no ranking, scoring, preference, candidate compilation, route selection, provider/model priority, dispatch, or budget behavior
no transport, delivery, batching, acknowledgment, receipt, quorum, transcript, or lifecycle behavior
no identity proof, authentication, credential, signature, evidence, trust, policy authorization, or enforcement claim
no tool invocation, runtime execution, side effect, production compatibility, or product capability claim
no merge, publication, deployment, activation, or release authority
